privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page says what the platform collects, why, how long it keeps it, and what rights a member has.
privacy.basisBody: Members' data is processed on the basis of the employment relationship and the org's legitimate interest in running its knowledge sessions and recording attendance. This is not a consumer service and it is not offered to the public: an account exists because the person belongs to an org on the platform.
privacy.collectIntro: Nothing beyond what a stated requirement needs. This is all of it:
privacy.collectIdentity: Name, avatar and email from the Google account on first sign-in — for identity and notification.
privacy.collectProfile: Company, job title, bio and interests — for leaderboards and discovery, written by the member.
privacy.collectActivity: RSVPs, check-ins, comments, photos, ratings, the points ledger and certificates — the product itself.
privacy.collectCalendar: Google Calendar tokens, if a member connects their calendar. The scope is event-write only; we do not read your calendar's contents.
privacy.collectAudit: IP address and user agent on audit rows — for security, not for behavioural tracking and not for advertising.
privacy.notCollectBody: No phone number, home address, national ID, salary, management hierarchy, location beyond the session's venue, and no advertising identifiers. EXIF and GPS data are stripped from every photo before it is stored.
privacy.visibilityRatings: The ratings you write are shown to no presenter and no member. That is what keeps them honest.
privacy.visibilityAbsence: No-shows and late cancellations are visible to the org admin alone, and to the person they describe.
privacy.visibilityAttendance: Sessions you attended are not shown to other members. Sessions you presented are — the platform surfaces what you stood up to say, not what you sat down to hear.
privacy.visibilityCalendar: Calendar tokens are hidden from the org admin too. A token is a credential for a personal account, not org data.
privacy.retentionIntro: Every class has a period, and every period has a scheduled job that enforces it. The periods live in a table the system reads, not as numbers written into code:
privacy.retentionCheckin: Check-in attempts, including failures: ninety days.
privacy.retentionEmail: Email delivery logs: one hundred and eighty days.
privacy.retentionLedger: Points ledger: the life of the org. It is not trimmed, because it is what every balance is recomputed from; trimming it would break the ability to verify a balance at all.
privacy.retentionContent: Sessions, materials, comments and photos: the life of the org.
privacy.retentionCalendar: Calendar tokens: deleted immediately on disconnect, not after a period.
privacy.retentionExport: Self-service export archives: seven days, then the contents are erased.
privacy.rightsAccess: Access: you can export everything the platform holds about you, machine-readable, from the privacy page in your account.
privacy.rightsCorrect: Correction: your profile fields are yours to edit at any time.
privacy.rightsErase: Erasure: you request deactivation, an org admin performs it, and your personal data is anonymised after twelve months.
privacy.rightsEraseHonest: Said plainly: there is no immediate self-service deletion. What you wrote is depended on by other members — a pre-read someone is preparing with, a comment that opened a thread — and deleting it tears holes in pages that are not only yours. Anonymisation serves the purpose without that: your personal data is erased, what you wrote stays attributed to a former member, and your ledger rows keep a pseudonymous id so the org's balances still reconcile.
privacy.securityBody: Isolation between orgs is enforced in the database rather than in application code: a query that forgets its predicate returns no row from another org. A platform admin cannot read an org's data at all; reaching in takes a session capped at four hours that is written to that org's own audit log, where its admins can see it.
privacy.breachBody: If a security incident affects personal data, the affected org and the competent authority are notified as the law requires, and an incident record documents what happened and what was done.
privacy.pdplBody: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law applies to this processing. The platform states its lawful basis, limits its purpose, minimises what it collects, supports access, correction and erasure, states retention periods, describes its security measures and provides for breach notification — each of them described above rather than referred to.
privacy.transferBody: The database and storage are currently hosted in ap-southeast-1 (Singapore), and the email and error-reporting providers are outside the Kingdom.
privacy.transferHonest: This is recorded as a fact to revisit, not as a legal conclusion. This page does not conclude that the current arrangement is compliant, and it does not conclude that it is not; that is a legal determination for the platform's owner, not an architectural one. The region is a configuration choice: nothing in the architecture assumes Singapore, and moving is an operational project rather than a redesign.
privacy.contactBody: For any question about your data, start with your org's admin: they are responsible for their members' data and they are who performs a deactivation request.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Short terms, because what they govern is simple: an internal platform for knowledge sessions among the employees of participating orgs.
terms.accessBody: Sign in with a Google account on a domain your org has allowed. There is no self-registration for orgs or individuals: a platform admin creates the org, and its admin manages its members. An account belongs to one org and does not move between them.
terms.conductBody: That what you post is your own work or properly attributed, that it carries no confidential data of your org or its clients, and that it respects whoever reads it. Admins and moderators may remove content that does not, and every removal is written to the audit log.
terms.contentBody: Ownership of what you upload stays with you or your org as agreed between you; you grant the platform what it needs to display it inside your org, convert it for viewing, and include it in the posters and certificates attached to your session. None of it is shown outside your org.
terms.uploadsBody: Uploads are sniffed on content, not on extension. SVG is not accepted in any upload path, because it is a scriptable document that would render inside a privileged browser on the conversion server. Each org sets its own size limits.
terms.certificatesBody: Certificates are issued from a recorded check-in or an accepted presenting role. Each carries a serial and a verification code that works without signing in. An admin may revoke one with a stated reason; a revocation is recorded and the file is not deleted.
terms.availabilityBody: The platform is provided as it is, with no guarantee of uninterrupted availability. An org may be suspended by a platform admin; its data is retained and suspension is reversible. Deletion is a separate act: irreversible, and recorded.
terms.changesBody: This page may change. A material change is announced inside the platform before it takes effect.
